note: Quantities like mass or velocity, not units.

answers.label: Mass
answers.desc: property of matter to resist changes of the state of motion and to attract other bodies

answers.label: Distance
answers.desc: length of straight line that connects two points in a measurable space or in an observable physical space

answers.label: Displacement
answers.desc: vector that is the shortest distance from the initial to the final position of a point P

answers.label: Depth
answers.desc: horizontal dimension away from the observer

answers.label: Area
answers.desc: measure of the extent of a two-dimensional region on a curved surface or flat plane

answers.label: Velocity
answers.desc: rate of change of the position of an object as a function of time, and the direction of that change

answers.label: Acceleration
answers.desc: rate at which the magnitude and/or direction of velocity changes with time

answers.label: Force
answers.desc: physical influence that tends to cause an object to change motion unless opposed by other forces

answers.label: Momentum
answers.desc: conserved physical quantity related to the motion of a body

answers.label: Impulse
answers.desc: integral of a force over the time interval for which it acts; term in classical mechanics

answers.label: Energy
answers.desc: quantitative property of a physical system, recognizable in the performance of work and in the form of heat and light

answers.label: Work
answers.desc: energy transferred to an object via the application of force on it through a displacement

answers.label: Power
answers.desc: rate at which energy is transferred, used, or transformed

answers.label: Heat
answers.desc: energy that is transferred from one body to another as the result of a difference in temperature

answers.label: Specific heat capacity
answers.desc: intensive quantity, heat capacity per mass

answers.label: Latent heat
answers.desc: released or absorbed energy during a constant-temperature process

answers.label: Enthalpy
answers.desc: measure of energy in a thermodynamic system; thermodynamic quantity equivalent to the total heat content of a system

answers.label: Capacitance
answers.desc: ability of a body to store electrical charge

answers.label: Inductance
answers.desc: property of electrical conductors to oppose changes in current flow

answers.label: Frequency
answers.desc: number of occurrences or cycles per time

answers.label: Wavelength
answers.desc: spatial period of the wave; the distance over which the wave's shape repeats; the inverse of the spatial frequency

answers.label: Amplitude
answers.desc: physical quantity; (of a periodic variable) measure of its change over a single period (such as time or spatial period)

answers.label: Period
answers.desc: smallest temporal unit after which a process repeats

answers.label: Magnetic flux
answers.desc: surface integral of the magnetic flux density

answers.label: Illuminance
answers.desc: luminous flux incident on a surface per area

answers.label: Moment
answers.desc: product of a distance and a physical quantity

answers.label: Angular velocity
answers.desc: physical quantity defined as the rate of change of angular position whose direction is (if regarded as a vector) the axis of rotation

answers.label: Angular momentum
answers.desc: measure of the extent to which an object will continue to rotate in the absence of an applied torque

answers.label: Moment of inertia
answers.desc: scalar measure of the rotational inertia with respect to a fixed axis of rotation

answers.label: Activity
answers.desc: physical quantity in nuclear physics, measured in becquerel, revealing the average number of nucleuses experiencing a spontaneous reaction per second

answers.label: Refractive index
answers.desc: ratio of the speed of light in vacuum to that in the medium

answers.label: Focal length
answers.desc: measure of how strongly an optical system converges or diverges light

answers.label: Intensity
answers.desc: power transferred per unit area, where the area is measured on the plane perpendicular to the direction of propagation of the energy

answers.label: Pitch
answers.desc: perceptual property in music ordering sounds from low to high

answers.label: Spin
answers.desc: intrinsic form of angular momentum as a property of quantum particles

answers.label: Surface tension
answers.desc: tendency of a liquid surface to shrink to reduce surface area

answers.label: Mass number
answers.desc: number of heavy particles in the atomic nucleus

answers.label: Atomic number
answers.desc: number of protons found in the nucleus of an atom
